page.title: Best Projector with Roku Built In (2026): 5 Roku TV Projectors Compared
page.h1: Best projector with Roku built in
page.desc: The VANKYO H500R gives native 1080p and 330 ANSI lumens with Roku TV inside. We compare it with Aurzen's tested D1R, D1R Cube and D1R air, plus the cheapest Roku TV projector.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best projector with Roku built in is the VANKYO Performance H500R ({buy:vankyo-performance-h500r-roku-tv}): native 1080p and 330 ANSI lumens with Roku TV inside, 50 lumens more than the Aurzen EAZZE D1R at the same price. A dim picture is the top complaint about every Roku projector, so plan on a dark room. With the lights off, the H500R fills a 100-inch screen from about 9 feet.

Roku TV built in means Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube and The Roku Channel run on the projector with a normal Roku remote. You don't need a stick. In the US, only VANKYO and Aurzen sell Roku TV projectors right now. The H500R lists the same 330 ANSI lumens, 1.23:1 throw ratio and two 5 W speakers as the Aurzen EAZZE D1R Cube, which costs $249.99. The catch is that no independent reviewer has measured the H500R yet. If you want a model reviewers have tested, the Aurzen EAZZE D1R costs $199.99 and is rated at 280 ANSI lumens. Expert Reviews measured its fan at 44 dBA and called it barely audible.

These are movie projectors, not gaming projectors. lon.tv measured about a quarter second of input lag on the D1R Cube. Prices were seen on the VANKYO and Aurzen stores on 2026-11-11.

cells.best: Tested by reviewers, quiet fan (44 dBA measured)
Sealed optical engine for dusty rooms

page.after:
What owners and reviewers complain about

  • Brightness (6 of 7 reviews we read). Every Roku TV projector here is rated at 150 to 330 lumens. Reviewers say you need closed curtains, and daytime viewing is hard.
  • Input lag (3 of 7). lon.tv measured about 0.25 seconds on the D1R Cube, and Android Authority wouldn't game on the D1R. Use a TV for fast games.
  • Fan noise (2 of 7, and reviewers disagree). Android Authority called the D1R fan fairly loud. Notebookcheck found it louder in bright scenes and quieter in Low Power mode. Expert Reviews measured 44 dBA and called it barely audible.
  • Built-in Roku is slower than a stick (2 reviews). It works fine but feels less snappy than a current Roku stick.
  • Smaller gripes. The remote isn't backlit and has no voice button (Expert Reviews). There's no tilting stand on the D1R (Android Authority). The D1R's light engine isn't fully dust-sealed (Notebookcheck). One VANKYO 570 owner at Best Buy had to re-enter the Wi-Fi password a few times.

Which one by need

  • Living-room movie nights, about $200: VANKYO H500R ({buy:vankyo-performance-h500r-roku-tv}). It has the most rated light at this price. It's new, so the tested choice is the Aurzen EAZZE D1R at the same price.
  • Dusty room or long-term use: Aurzen EAZZE D1R Cube ($249.99). It has the H500R's listed specs plus a sealed optical engine.
  • Backyard or travel: Aurzen EAZZE D1R air ($239.99). It runs on USB-C power, weighs 2.6 lb and is rated at 300 ANSI lumens.
  • Lowest price, kid's room or ceiling: VANKYO Leisure 3R Air ({buy:vankyo-leisure-3r-air-roku-tv}). It's 720p and rated at 150 lumens, so keep the picture at 60 to 80 inches in a dark room.

Not recommended

  • VANKYO Leisure 470 with Roku Express ($125.99): Roku comes as a stick in the box, not built in. It's rated at 120 ANSI lumens and costs more than the 3R Air.
  • Any of these for gaming or a bright room: about a quarter second of lag and 330 lumens at most. A TV does both jobs better.

notes:
QUERY: 'projector with roku built in' is Google's top autocomplete for 'projector with roku'. Other suggestions are 'projector with roku tv' and 'roku projector review/4k/screen'. Today's results are thin: mostly affiliate roundups on unrelated domains such as talkofthehouse, peggyomara and beatcopgame, plus brand blogs.

PAIN POINTS (7 editorial reviews plus Best Buy snippets): brightness / needs a dark room 6 of 7. Input lag 3 (lon.tv about 0.25 s on the D1R Cube; Android Authority; lon.tv D1R). Fan noise 2 negative (Android Authority, Notebookcheck) against Expert Reviews' 44 dBA 'barely audible' and 2 Best Buy owners saying it's fine. Built-in Roku slower than a stick 2. Remote not backlit / no voice 1. No tilt stand 1. D1R engine not dust-sealed 1. Wi-Fi forgotten on a VANKYO 570, 1 Best Buy owner. Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy review pages were blocked or timed out, so I couldn't count owner reviews directly.

SEGMENTS AND WINNERS: (1) Most light for about $200: VANKYO H500R, 330 ANSI and 1080p at $199.99, against the Aurzen D1R's 280 ANSI at $199.99. (2) Tested pick at the same price: Aurzen D1R. (3) Sealed optics: Aurzen D1R Cube at $249.99, which lists the same 330 ANSI, 1.23:1 throw, 2×5 W, 7×7.4×7.8 in and 4 lb as the H500R. That suggests a shared platform, but it isn't confirmed, and the page only says 'same listed specs'. (4) Portable: Aurzen D1R air, 300 ANSI, USB-C, 2.6 lb, $239.99. (5) Lowest price: VANKYO Leisure 3R Air at $119.99, 720p, 150 lumens.

EARNING: Both VANKYO records are awin:vankyo. The Aurzen D1R, D1R Cube and D1R air are cj:aurzen (an approved brand) but aren't in products.py. Brand mode limits records to VANKYO's own, so they appear as unlinked maker rows with dated prices. Adding cj:aurzen records for them later would earn on segments 2 to 4. No Amazon records.

VERIFIED 2026-11-11: VANKYO store search feed (storecheck search): H500R $199.99 in stock, 3R Air $119.99 in stock, Leisure 470 with Roku Express $125.99. Store text confirms native 1080P, Roku TV, 2×5 W and Bluetooth 5.2 for the H500R, and 150 lumens, 720P and 38-200 in for the 3R Air. The H500R's compare_at of $198 is below its price, so I left out list_price. Aurzen store search feed: D1R $199.99 (280 ANSI in store text), D1R Cube $249.99 ('Sealed Optical Engine' in store text), D1R air $239.99 ('USB-C Powered', 'Native 1080P, 300 ANSI'), E1R $139.99. VANKYO policies read today: 1-year projector warranty (an older search snippet said 24 months, which is outdated), 30-day returns, ships to the contiguous US only, ships from an operator listed in Hong Kong. The home page banner shows only 'Fast, Free Delivery'. No codes on the brand site, and the network listed none.

NOT VERIFIED ON THE MAKER PAGE: storecheck product and WebFetch both got HTTP 429 from ivankyo.com and aurzen.com product pages all session. That leaves several figures without a maker-page check. H500R 330 ANSI comes from VANKYO's own launch release, plus Notebookcheck and ProjectorCentral. H500R 1.23:1 throw, 32 dB, 7.0×7.4×7.8 in and about 4 lb come from ProjectorCentral. D1R Cube 330 ANSI comes from ProjectorCentral, and D1R air 2.6 lb from ProjectorCentral. We also couldn't confirm whether the store's H500R includes a screen (Best Buy's H500RS bundle does) or whether its optics are sealed, so the page claims neither. The 3R Air weight conflicts (15.5 oz in the 3R press release, 2.5 lb on ProjectorCentral) and is left off.
